purpose: Reference prototype patterns for embedding-space dietary-pattern resemblance scoring. Each prototype is anchored to a published literature reference, with 3-5 hand-curated example days that span the variation the source paper documents. The classifier builds a mass-weighted day vector from CNF + WAFCT food embeddings (cnf_corpus_embeddings.npz) for each example_day, averages within a prototype to get the prototype vector, then computes cosine to a user's day vector.
curation_note: FoodIDs verified against backend pipeline 2026-05-24. CNF FoodIDs < 700,000; WAFCT FoodIDs >= 700,000. Where a perfect CNF analogue is missing (e.g. fresh fruit not in CNF as raw), a WAFCT entry is substituted with a comment.

prototypes.literature_anchor: Trichopoulou A, Costacou T, Bamia C, Trichopoulos D. Adherence to a Mediterranean diet and survival in a Greek population. NEJM 2003;348:2599-2608. Estruch R, Ros E, Salas-Salvadó J, et al. Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease with a Mediterranean Diet. NEJM 2013;368:1279-1290 (PREDIMED).
prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: PREDIMED: composite CVD HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.54-0.92) over 4.8 y; Trichopoulou: 25% lower all-cause mortality top vs bottom quintile of adherence.
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Lots of olive oil, vegetables, legumes, fish, and whole grains, with moderate dairy and less red meat than a typical Western diet.

prototypes.literature_anchor: Sacks FM, Svetkey LP, Vollmer WM, et al. Effects on Blood Pressure of Reduced Dietary Sodium and the DASH Diet. NEJM 2001;344:3-10. Appel LJ, Moore TJ, Obarzanek E, et al. A Clinical Trial of the Effects of Dietary Patterns on Blood Pressure. NEJM 1997;336:1117-1124.
prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: DASH vs control: systolic BP -5.5 mmHg (-7.4 to -3.7) at low Na (Sacks 2001 Table 3). Hypertensive subgroup: -11.5/-5.7 mmHg.
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Plenty of vegetables, fruit, low-fat dairy, whole grains, and lean protein, with limited salt and red meat. Built to support healthy blood pressure.

prototypes.literature_anchor: Krebs-Smith SM, Reedy J, Bosire C. Healthfulness of the U.S. food supply: little improvement despite decades of dietary guidance. Am J Prev Med 2010;38(5):472-477. NHANES 2015-2018 mean intake distribution (Brassard 2022b reports a comparable Canadian mean HEFI = 43.1/80, Table A2 p. 591).
prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: Comparator baseline — NO positive outcome claim. Higher Western adherence associates with higher CVD/T2D incidence in cohort studies (cited e.g. Hu 2002 Curr Opin Lipidol 13:3 for the original PCA-derived Western pattern definition).
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Refined grains, red and processed meat, sweets, sugary drinks, and packaged snacks. A common North American pattern used for comparison, not as a goal.

example_days.name: American fast-food day (~2400 kcal, high added sugar + Na)

prototypes.literature_anchor: Orlich MJ, Singh PN, Sabaté J, et al. Vegetarian dietary patterns and mortality in Adventist Health Study 2. JAMA Intern Med 2013;173(13):1230-1238.
prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: Adventist Health Study 2 (N=73,308): vegetarian vs nonvegetarian all-cause mortality HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.80-0.97); lacto-ovo vegetarian HR 0.91.
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Mostly plant foods with dairy and eggs, and no meat, poultry, or fish. Healthfulness still depends on how much processed food is included.

example_days.name: Lacto-ovo balanced day with whole grains + legumes

prototypes.literature_anchor: Orlich MJ, Singh PN, Sabaté J, et al. Vegetarian dietary patterns and mortality in Adventist Health Study 2. JAMA Intern Med 2013;173(13):1230-1238 (vegan subgroup).
prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: Adventist Health Study 2 vegan subgroup all-cause mortality HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.73-1.01). Note: Adventist cohort is healthier than general population, so absolute risk reductions may not generalise.
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Plant foods only, with no animal products. Legumes, tofu, and fortified plant drinks often carry much of the protein and key nutrients.

prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: Not outcome-validated (Brassard 2022b Discussion p. 589 explicitly: 'link between HEFI-2019 and disease endpoints is undetermined'); descriptive comparator anchored to the top quintile of the Canadian population (HEFI ≥ 65/80 per Brassard 2022b Table A2 p. 591).
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Half the plate vegetables and fruit, whole grains, varied protein with an emphasis on plants, and water as the main drink. Matches Canada's Food Guide 2019.

prototypes.literature_anchor: Vincent A, Grande F, Compaoré E, et al. FAO/INFOODS Food Composition Table for Western Africa (WAFCT 2019). Rome: FAO; 2019 — sheet 09 mixed-dish canonical recipes (195 recipes documented across Burkina Faso / Mali / Senegal / Nigeria + regional staples).

prototypes.literature_anchor: Rockström J, Thilsted SH, Willett WC, et al. The EAT-Lancet Commission on healthy, sustainable, and just food systems (EAT-Lancet 2.0). Lancet 2025;406(10510):1625-1700. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(25)01201-2. Direct successor to: Willett W, Rockström J, Loken B, et al. Food in the Anthropocene (EAT-Lancet 1.0). Lancet 2019;393:447-492.
prototypes.literature_anchor_2025_revision_note: EAT-Lancet 2.0 (Rockström 2025, Table 1 p. 1632) revises the Planetary Health Diet (PHD) reference intake to ~2400 kcal/day (down from 2500 kcal/day in the 2019 Commission, p. 1636). Macronutrient profile: ~14% energy from protein, ~53% from carbohydrate, ~35% from total fat; added/free sugar capped at 5% of energy; sodium <2 g/day (Table 1 p. 1637). Headline composition shifts vs 2019: whole grains widened from 232 g/d to 210 g/d (with 20-50% energy range), legumes widened to 75 g/d (0-150 range), beef/pork/lamb narrowed to 15 g/d (0-30), poultry at 30 g/d (0-60), fish at 30 g/d (0-100). The 2025 update also publishes food-system planetary boundaries (Table 2 p. 1640) for the first time.
prototypes.outcome_evidence_reused: EAT-Lancet 2.0 (Rockström 2025, Panel 1 p. 1629): PHD adoption projected to prevent ~10 million deaths/yr via the comparative risk assessment method (17% of total mortality), or ~15 million deaths/yr (27%) via the PHD-index pattern method on a >200,000-adult cohort with >30-yr follow-up. Highest-decile PHD adherence = 28% lower overall mortality vs lowest decile (n=206,404; >54,000 deaths). NOTE: targets are aspirational and population-level, NOT personal-risk predictions.
prototypes.individual_mode_blurb: Mostly plants, modest fish, very little red meat, dairy, and added sugar, with half the plate vegetables and fruit. Aimed at both health and planetary limits.

example_days.source_section: Rockström 2025 Table 1 p. 1632 (revised reference daily intake at 2400 kcal/day)
